series.title: Speculators in WTI
series.vintage: CFTC legacy Commitments of Traders, NYMEX WTI futures. Data through October 13, 2026.
series.narrative_text: Noncommercial traders, the speculative category in the legacy Commitments of Traders report, hold a net long of 100,343 contracts in NYMEX WTI futures as of October 13, 2026, in the 4th percentile of weekly readings since 2015. The position grew by 1,283 contracts on the week. Positioning is the crowdedness gauge for the outright: a stretched net long is flush fuel on any bearish surprise, and a stretched net short is squeeze fuel the other way. A move back toward the middle of the range would stand this read down.

series.title: Managed money in Brent
series.source: ICE Futures Europe Commitments of Traders
series.vintage: ICE Futures Europe Commitments of Traders, Brent futures only. Data through October 13, 2026.
series.narrative_text: Managed money holds a net long of 206,930 contracts in ICE Brent futures as of October 13, 2026, in the 55th percentile of weekly readings since 2020, up 20,642 contracts on the week. Brent positioning is the global book's tell: it moves the whole crude complex, including the differentials struck off it. A washout toward flat, or a build into crowded territory, would each change what this chart is saying.

series.title: U.S. crude oil inventories
series.vintage: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report. Data through October 16, 2026.
series.narrative_text: U.S. crude oil inventories stand at 412.5 million barrels, 28.6 million barrels (6.5 percent) below the ten-year seasonal average, a gap of 1.2 standard deviations, and in the 32nd percentile of readings for this part of the year since 2010. Stocks drew 3.1 million barrels on the week. Crude is the master stock: sustained draws against the seasonal average are the tightening signal the whole complex prices off, and the level behind every prompt spread. Two or three weekly builds back toward the average would retire the tightening read.

series.title: Cushing inventories
series.vintage: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report. Data through October 16, 2026.
series.narrative_text: Cushing inventories stand at 27.6 million barrels, 10.5 million barrels (27.6 percent) below the ten-year seasonal average, a gap of 0.6 standard deviations, and in the 36th percentile of readings for this part of the year since 2010. Stocks built 1.0 million barrels on the week. Cushing, Oklahoma is the WTI delivery point: its level against the seasonal average is the prompt WTI spread story in one number, and it caps how bearish the outright can trade. A rebuild toward the seasonal average would ease the prompt tightness a low reading implies.

series.title: U.S. gasoline inventories

series.vintage: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, via the stack EIA pull. Data through October 16, 2026.
series.narrative_text: U.S. gasoline inventories stand at 205.3 million barrels, 14.4 million barrels (6.6 percent) below the ten-year seasonal average, a gap of 2.0 standard deviations, and in the 14th percentile of readings for this part of the year since 2010. Stocks drew 3.0 million barrels on the week. Gasoline stocks set the summer crack tone and, into the autumn shoulder, the pace at which refiners can ease runs: a low seasonal percentile is refinery-margin support. A seasonal build through the shoulder months would close the tightness case.

series.narrative_text: U.S. distillate inventories stand at 104.3 million barrels, 22.6 million barrels (17.8 percent) below the ten-year seasonal average, a gap of 1.3 standard deviations, and in the 4th percentile of readings for this part of the year since 2010. series.title: WTI front month
series.vintage: Exchange front-month futures, via the daily crack file. Data through October 22, 2026.
series.narrative_text: WTI front month closed at $99.88 on October 22, 2026, in the 94th percentile of daily closes since 2020 and +5.29 dollars over the last thirty days. The outright is context rather than the trade: the differentials and calendar spreads this site follows are struck off this level, and its trend sets the tone they trade in. A sustained break of the recent range, either way, would reset that context.

series.title: WCS differential at Hardisty
series.vintage: Natural Resources Canada selected crude prices. Data through August 31, 2026; TMW settle from ICE daily settlements.
series.narrative_text: The assessed WCS discount at Hardisty was $18.57 a barrel in the last published reading, August 31, 2026 (Natural Resources Canada publishes monthly, about two months in arrears), in the 73rd percentile of daily assessments since 2021. The tradable edge moves faster: the ICE WCS 1A index future (TMW) for December 2026 settled at -$28.35 on October 21, 2026. The assessed series is the slow, official record of what the basis did; the TMW settle is what it costs to trade it now. A narrowing of the assessed discount toward twelve dollars, or a blowout past twenty-five, would each rewrite this block.

series.title: 3-2-1 crack spread
series.vintage: Computed daily from front-month WTI, RBOB gasoline, and heating oil futures. Data through October 22, 2026.
series.narrative_text: The 3-2-1 crack spread printed $52.30 a barrel on October 22, 2026, in the 91st percentile of daily readings since 2020. The crack is the refining system's margin: at this level refiners run as hard as equipment allows, which is crude demand support, and product supply eventually answers. A crack back under twenty-five dollars would signal margin-driven run cuts and soften the crude bid.

series.title: Alberta crude inventories
series.vintage: AER ST3, Alberta crude closing inventories. Data through August 2026.
series.narrative_text: Alberta crude inventories stand at 60.0 million barrels, 3.4 million barrels (5.3 percent) below the ten-year seasonal average, a gap of 0.5 standard deviations, and in the 62nd percentile of readings for this part of the year since 2010. Stocks built 1.3 million barrels on the month. This is the basin's buffer, and the earliest physical read on whether egress is keeping up with supply: what cannot leave accumulates here. It is also the print the satellite shadow read on Tank Watch is scored against, two months before ST3 publishes. A draw back to the seasonal average over the next two prints would retire the build story.

series.title: Crude exports vs egress capacity
series.source: Canada Energy Regulator; site egress model
series.pull: feed-cer-throughput-monthly (bin/pull_cer.py); egress stack from the S&D model
series.vintage: CER crude oil exports by type (total). Data through June 2026; capacity from the site egress model's demonstrated stack.
series.narrative_text: Canadian crude exports averaged 4,616 thousand barrels a day in June 2026, the latest Canada Energy Regulator print, against a demonstrated egress capacity stack of 4,984 thousand barrels a day in the site's egress model: roughly 368 thousand barrels a day of headroom. Exports are what the pipes and rails exist to carry. When this line presses the capacity line, apportionment rises and the differential widens; supply growth that closes the gap, or a capacity step that widens it, changes the read.

series.title: Mainline apportionment
series.vintage: Enbridge apportionment notices, as pinned in apportionment_seen.json. Latest: November 2026.
series.narrative_text: Enbridge set November 2026 Mainline apportionment at 19 percent for light crude and 7 percent for heavy at Kerrobert, against 8 and 4 percent in October. Apportionment is the basin's congestion price in percentage form: it is the share of nominated barrels the pipe cannot take, and it leads the differential when it steps. The full history and the prediction scoring record are on the Apportionment page. A return to zero would say the pressure has cleared; another step up would say the squeeze is still building.

series.title: Managed money in the TMW diff
series.vintage: CFTC Disaggregated Commitments of Traders, ICE WCS 1A index future. Data through October 13, 2026.
series.narrative_text: Managed money is net short 19,415 contracts in the ICE WCS 1A index future (TMW) as of October 13, 2026, in the 3rd percentile of weekly readings since 2024, with speculative shorts at 25.0 percent of open interest. This is the crowding gauge inside the differential itself: a heavily short speculative position is squeeze fuel if the diff tightens on apportionment, an outage, or a storage surprise. A cover back toward flat would remove the fuel, and a fresh build of shorts would add to it.

series.title: TD3C tanker earnings
series.vintage: Baltic Exchange via freight pull. Data through October 09, 2026.

stats.trigger: In rotation: TD3C earnings at a series record, $1,412,594 a day

series.narrative_text: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) earnings on the Middle East to China route, TD3C, printed $1,412,594 a day in the week of October 09, 2026 (Worldscale 1,319), in the 100th percentile of weekly readings since March 2024. Freight at this level is a tax on every long-haul barrel and reshuffles which grades can travel; the Freight Watch page tracks it route by route, including the Vancouver to Asia leg that prices TMX barrels. Four consecutive weeks back inside the normal band retires this chart to the archive below.
